field.name: disabled

entity.description: A service that answers where a connection of a kind is used, beside the kind's own answer: the owner of the records that name it (Mantle's gateways and store integrations naming a remote, facilities naming a printer). It implements org.moqui.admin.ConfigurationServices.find#AdapterConsumers; seed data, as ConnectionAdapter.

What Admin knows of one connection beside its native record: the last explicit test (test#Connection) with its safe diagnostics, the mark of a passing test (the fingerprint of the endpoint fields it ran against, never a secret, by whom and when), whether the connection waits for a test because its endpoint changed, and whether that change cleared a stored secret that has not been entered again (no test sends anything until it is). Written by ConfigurationServices only. The last result of a protocol check (test#Protocol, impl-admin P12) is kept here too, under the adapter key protocol and the protocol's and check's keys.

field.name: pendingTest
field.description: Y: disabled by the endpoint-change rule (or new), so a passing test enables it; a connection an administrator disabled stays disabled after a test

field.name: secretCleared
field.description: Y: an endpoint change cleared a stored secret and none has been entered since

field.name: lastCheckText
field.description: The checks of the last test as JSON: each a name, ok or failed and a text that names hosts and statuses, never a secret or a response body

entity.description: A registered owner of mail send outcomes (org.moqui.admin.OperationServices.find#MailOutcomes): a component whose own ledger holds the attempts of messages it sends (Mantle's delivery ledger) seeds a row, so the mail queue never retries or settles such a message beside its owner. ownerService answers which of a list of EmailMessages are its own, with their state at the owner (it implements OperationServices.find#MailOutcomeOwners); recoverService, when it names one, is the owner's own retry and reconciliation of such a message (OperationServices.recover#OwnedMailOutcome), which checks the owner's permission itself: the registration adds no right. A row naming a service that is not there is logged by name when read and left out, and every message is then held for its owner (no retry here) until it answers.

What an operation of org.moqui.admin.OperationServices answered, by the operation key its caller gave (a retry, a reconciliation; later a recovery action): a repeat of the request with the same key answers the first result and does nothing again. A key is one operation's: one kind, one target, one user. The result is the service's safe answer (no secret, address, subject or body). Written by OperationServices only.

A registered recovery of one kind of operational record (org.moqui.admin.OperationServices preview#Recovery and execute#Recovery): its owner seeds a row, and without one nothing is retried, settled or cancelled from there. targetKind is the kind of record (SystemMessage; ServiceJob, a scheduled job, whose targetKey is the jobName and whose retry is a run outside its schedule) and targetKey what of that kind the row covers (for SystemMessage the systemMessageTypeId), with direction (in, out, or empty for both) for a message. Each action has a mode: native (the framework's own action on the record, which the owner hereby says is safe to repeat: the receiver or the consuming service answers the same record once), owner (recoverService, the owner's own service, implementing OperationServices.recover#OwnedTarget, which checks the owner's permission and scope itself) or empty (not offered). retryStates narrows the states a retry is offered in. managePermission is the owner's permission an actor needs besides ADMIN_OPERATION_MANAGE, and dataPermission the one a reader needs to be shown the record's payload. describeService, when named (OperationServices.find#RecoveryTargets), answers per record what its owner would take now, whether its outcome is unknown there, and whether this reader may see its diagnostics and payload. The registration adds no right. A row naming a service that is not defined is logged by name when read and left out, and its records are then offered nothing.

field.name: direction
field.description: in, out or empty (both)

field.name: retryMode
field.description: native, owner or empty

field.name: reconcileMode
field.description: native, owner or empty

field.name: cancelMode
field.description: native, owner or empty

field.name: retryStates
field.description: The states a retry is offered in, comma separated; empty for the kind's own (a message: failed, retrying)

field.name: idempotencyNote
field.description: What makes a repeat safe, in words, shown before an action is confirmed

field.name: ownerRoute
field.description: The owner's own place for such a record, as a key the application showing it resolves (never a URL)

field.name: itemsService
field.description: For a job (targetKind ServiceJob, targetKey the jobName): the owner's service answering the independent items of one run (OperationServices.find#JobRunItems), which checks the owner's permission and scope itself

entity.description: A handler a message type may be given in delegated administration (org.moqui.admin.ConfigurationServices.store#MessageType): the type's owner seeds a row for each service that may send (handlerRole send) or consume (consume) messages of that one type. store#MessageType sets a type's send or consume service only to a handler registered for that type and role, by its key, never to a service name from the request; a type with no row here is not changed there at all. The service that receives a type's messages is never chosen there. A row naming a service that is not defined is logged by name when read and left out.

field.name: handlerRole
field.description: send or consume

entity.description: A scheduled job (moqui.service.job.ServiceJob) its owner registers for delegated administration (org.moqui.admin.OperationServices.store#Job): without a row a job is read only there. The row says which of the job's scheduling controls may be changed: its schedule (scheduleEditable, with minIntervalMinutes, the shortest time between two runs a schedule set there may have), its pause (pauseEditable), its priority (priorityEditable) and its wait after an error (retryEditable). Its parameters are changed only where a JobParameterDefinition registers one, and its notification recipients only when recipientPermission names the permission a recipient must hold (a job's notification carries the run's errors, parameters and results). managePermission is the owner's permission an actor needs besides ADMIN_OPERATION_MANAGE. The job's service, the identity it runs as, its topic, its time limits and its lock settings are the owner's deployment and are never changed there. A run outside the schedule is a registered recovery (RecoveryDescriptor, targetKind ServiceJob). The registration adds no right.

field.name: minIntervalMinutes
field.description: 1 when empty

field.name: ownerRoute
field.description: The owner's own place for the job's work, as a key the application showing it resolves (never a URL)

entity.description: A parameter of a registered job that is safe to change in delegated administration (OperationServices.store#Job): its owner seeds a row with the type its value has (valueType integer, decimal, boolean, option or text) and its bounds (minValue and maxValue of a number, optionValues comma separated, maxLength of a text). A text is letters, digits, spaces and . , : _ - only: never an expression, a path, a URL or an address. A parameter with no row is shown by name and never changed there; a row naming a parameter the job's service does not declare is logged by name when read and left out.

field.name: valueType
field.description: integer, decimal, boolean, option or text

field.name: maxLength
field.description: Of a text: 60 when empty, at most 255

field.name: required
field.description: If Y the parameter is never cleared

entity.description: A notification topic (moqui.security.user.NotificationTopic) its owner registers for delegated administration (OperationServices.store#TopicDefaults and store#TopicSubscription): without a row a topic is read only there. editableFields names, comma separated, the delivery settings that may be changed (description, showAlert, alertNoAutoHide, persistOnSend, receiveNotifications, emailNotifications, pushNotifications, digestDefault); a topic's title, error title and link templates, its email template, its approval services, its inbox and whether it is private are never changed there. subscriptionPermission is the topic's audience: the permission a user must hold for an administrator to set that user's subscription, and for the subscription to be listed by name; with none, no subscription is set there. Receiving every message of a topic (NotificationTopicUser.allNotifications) is never set there, only ended. The registration adds no right.

A registered target of a business data transfer (org.moqui.admin.DataTransferServices): its owner seeds a row, and without one nothing is staged, applied, exported or listed there. direction is import or export. An export target (impl-admin P16) has targetMode file (its owner's exportService, implementing DataTransferServices.run#TargetExport, writes a file of its own format), rows (the exportService answers rows and the file is written here, delimited text) or wizard (exported in its owner's own place: only ownerRoute is registered); for file and rows columnsJson names the only fields an export may hold (name, label, permission: what a caller must hold for the field to be written, comma separated; required; selected false for one left out unless asked for), optionsJson the options of a selection, scopeService the scopes a caller may export from, maxRows and maxBytes the bounds of one file (5000 rows and 2097152 bytes when empty, at most 50000 and 16777216; a larger one is refused whole), exportPermission what a caller must hold besides the owner's own checks, viewPermission who reads the records of others' exports, and retentionDays how long the record of an export is kept (366 when empty). For an import target targetMode says what the owner registers. steps: the owner keeps its own batch and names the five steps (stageService, configureService, validateService, applyService, getService, with an optional reportService, sampleService and kindsService), each carrying the import contract's parameters, as mantle.product.ProductImportServices. rows: the owner has no batch, and the framework keeps one (TransferBatch, TransferItem) for it: columnsJson names the only fields a row may carry (name, label, required, and permission: what a reader must hold, comma separated, to see the field's values in the staged rows and the report, masked for anyone else, and cleared from a row's staged values once it is applied), keyFields the fields that may not repeat in one file, optionsJson the options of a whole batch (name, label, type integer, text or option, with min, max, maxLength, options and default), refusedColumns words that refuse a file with such a column (beside the secret names every file is refused for), validateRowService (DataTransferServices.validate#TargetRow, which changes nothing) and applyRowService (apply#TargetRow, one row in a transaction of its own under an operation key), scopeService (find#TargetScopes: the scopes, such as organizations, the caller may import into and read), maxBytes and maxRows the bounds of a file and retentionDays how long a batch's staged rows are kept. wizard: the owner keeps its own wizard, and only its place (ownerRoute, a key the application showing it resolves, never a URL) is registered. For every mode findService (find#TargetRuns), when named, answers the owner's runs the caller may read there; a target with none and no batch here keeps no runs. importPermission and viewPermission name, comma separated, the permissions a caller must hold besides what the owner's services check themselves. fixedValuesJson holds values the registration gives every row's services (never from a request). The registration adds no right: an owner's service is called as the caller, under the caller's own authorization (call#TargetService). A row naming a service that is not defined, or one without its contract's parameters, is logged by name when read and left out.

field.name: direction
field.description: import

field.name: effectsNote
field.description: What applying it does, in words, shown before it is confirmed

field.name: targetMode
field.description: steps, rows or wizard

field.name: fieldLabel
field.description: What a field of the target is called in the wizard, such as Catalog field

field.name: stepFeatures
field.description: For steps: what its wizard offers, comma separated: kinds, updateMode, formats, clearFields, forceNew, sample

field.name: maxBytes
field.description: Of an import's file: 1048576 when empty, at most 2097152

field.name: maxRows
field.description: Of an import's file: 2000 when empty, at most 5000

field.name: retentionDays
field.description: 30 when empty

entity.description: One export of an export target (state exported: who, the target, scopeKey, the selection and field names in requestJson, rowCount, the file's name and the hash of its content, never the content; the record of the export, removed after the target's retention), or one import of a target that has no batch of its owner's (TransferTarget, targetMode rows), written by org.moqui.admin.DataTransferServices only. For an import: transferId is the import's operation key: the one its caller gave, or one made of the user, the target, the scope and the content's hash, so the same file staged again answers the same batch. scopeKey is the scope the import is for (an organization), userId who staged it: the batch and its rows are read by that user, and by a holder of the target's view permission whom the target's scope service admits. requestJson holds the file's headers, the mapping, defaults, value mappings and batch options; inputFingerprint the revision of the last validation, which an apply must name. state is staged, mapped, validated, applying, complete or partial. The staged rows are removed after the target's retention (purgedDate), the outcomes kept.

One row of a TransferBatch: what the file held (sourceJson), what validation made of it (previewJson: the values its apply would be given, warnings and the source's revision) and its outcome: result staged, valid, invalid, skipped, applied or failed, with the reason, the owner's reference of what it made (resultRef), the operation key its apply carried and the number of attempts. An applied row is never applied again.

A registered projection of the audit log (moqui.entity.EntityAuditLog) for org.moqui.admin.AuditServices.find#Changes: one field of one entity whose changes may be shown, and how. Its owner seeds a row; a change of an entity or a field with no row is never found, listed or counted there (the whole audit log is the instance administrator's, in Tools System's Audit). valueMode is show (the values before and after, as text) or marker (only that a value was set, changed or cleared; the default for anything else); a field the entity definition encrypts, or whose name reads as a secret, is a marker whatever its row says. sourceService is empty for a record of the whole instance (read here, by a holder of ADMIN_AUDIT_VIEW), or the service of the owner whose records belong to an organization (implementing AuditServices.find#OwnedChanges): it answers only the ids of the audit rows within the caller's own scope, and a row it does not answer is not shown. viewPermission, when set, is needed besides ADMIN_AUDIT_VIEW (comma separated, every one). primaryKeyKind and secondaryKeyKind say what a key value is, for its name: user (an account), group (a user group), plain (shown as it is) or hidden (never shown); primaryKeyTitle and secondaryKeyTitle are the words for them. linkKey names the owner's place for the record, which an app resolves to a route; never a path.

field.name: category
field.description: access, identity, signIn, configuration, connection, operation, transfer or backup.

entity.description: A readiness provider: a nonmutating check its owner calculates, read through ReadinessServices.get#Readiness by the Health screen, the support summary and the System home's attention list. The owner's service answers the contract: called with providerKey and the scope parameters the row names, it returns checks, each {checkKey, title, state (ready, warning, failed or unavailable), reasonCode, message, subject (whom or what it is for, in words), scope (the scope parameters that narrow to it), watermark, coverage, fixRoute, fixId, fixParameters}. It checks the caller's permission and scope itself and refuses with a reason code (PERMISSION_DENIED, RECORD_UNAVAILABLE and the like), which leaves the provider out; any other failure names it as not checked.

field.name: ownerApp
field.description: The app that owns the check, in words

field.name: healthGroupEnumId
field.description: The group it is shown in (AdminHealthGroup): identity, business setup, transport, storage and backup, observability

field.name: scopeEnumId
field.description: What one check covers, for display (AdminRegistryScope): the framework seeds the instance, an app adds its own (an organization, a store)

field.name: serviceName
field.description: The owner's service, answering the contract

field.name: requiredPermission
field.description: The permission the caller needs to read the provider, if any; the owner's service checks its own again

field.name: scopeParameters
field.description: The names of the scope parameters the owner's service takes from a request (comma separated), such as an organization: any other is dropped. The scope is the owner's to understand and to check. A provider that takes none of the scope a request names is left out of that request

field.name: fixRoute
field.description: The owner's place that fixes it, as a key the application showing it resolves (never a URL); a check may answer its own

field.name: fixId
field.description: The record the fix place opens, under the route's id parameter, if any

field.name: expectedFrequencyMinutes
field.description: The freshness facet of a data source: how often it should be refreshed

field.name: maxLagMinutes
field.description: The freshness facet: the lag past which the source is stale

entity.description: A refresh operation: the owner's service that refreshes a source (an index, a feed, a projection), run through ReadinessServices.request#Refresh by its key, never by a service or index name from a request. The owner's service is called with refreshKey, the operation key, the reason and the scope parameters the row names, and checks the caller's permission and scope itself.

field.name: sourceKindEnumId
field.description: index, feed or projection (AdminRefreshSource)

field.name: sourceName
field.description: The source it refreshes, as its owner names it

field.name: requiredPermission
field.description: The permission the caller needs to run it

field.name: scopeParameters
field.description: The names of the scope parameters passed to the owner's service from the request (comma separated); any other is dropped

field.name: providerKey
field.description: The readiness provider whose source it refreshes, for the Health screen's row action

entity.description: A settings entry: an owner's settings landing in the settings index (ReadinessServices.find#Settings), shown only to a caller whose own grants open its screen and who holds its view permission. The owner resolves scope and makes every change; the entry grants nothing. A component that shows the same settings in a screen of its own seeds the entry again under the same key with its own screenLocation.

field.name: settingsGroupEnumId
field.description: The index's group (AdminSettingsGroup): the framework seeds Applications and Instance, an app adds its own

field.name: scopeEnumId
field.description: What it applies to, for display (AdminRegistryScope)

field.name: destinationRoute
field.description: The settings' own place, as a key the application showing the index resolves (never a URL); an entry whose key has no route there is not shown there

field.name: screenLocation
field.description: The screen whose authorization decides whether the entry is shown: the caller's own grants must open it, counted down its component's screen directory as the framework counts a screen path (an always-allow or an inheritable allow above it, no deny). It need not be a file where the screen is mounted by location. An entry that names none is not shown

field.name: viewPermission
field.description: A permission the destination checks besides its screen authorization, if any

field.name: configuredBy
field.description: Who configures it, in the owner's words

field.name: providerKey
field.description: The readiness provider of what it configures, if any

entity.description: A host name an operator set up on System › Certificates to get its certificate from an ACME authority (Let's Encrypt by default). Nothing is ever requested for a name with no row. The order answers the authority's TLS-ALPN-01 challenge on the HTTPS listener (port 443 as the authority sees it), and the certificate is written in certbot's layout under runtime/cert/hostName/, which the listener reads. statusId is AcmeOrdering while an order runs, AcmeIssued after one succeeded and AcmeFailed after one failed (lastError says why). renewing is Y until the operator stops it: the renew_AcmeCertificates job then renews the name before notAfter. termsAgreedDate is when the operator agreed to the authority's terms.

The TLS-ALPN-01 challenge an order of hostName has open: the SHA-256 of its key authorization (hex), until expireDate. A row so that any member of a cluster answers it: a handshake that offers ALPN acme-tls/1 for the name gets a certificate made from it, and every other acme-tls/1 handshake is refused.
The certificate an ACME order of hostName got: its chain and its private key (PEM, the key encrypted), so every member of a cluster writes its own runtime/cert/hostName/fullchain.pem and privkey.pem.

The member of a cluster ordering hostName now, as ServiceJobRunLock is for a job: taken with the row locked, and taken over once leaseExpireDate has passed (by the clock of the member that looks, so members' clocks must agree within minutes of the 15-minute lease), so two members never order one name at once. A name left AcmeOrdering with no live lock was cut off by a stop and counts as failed.
